text.p: These are the leading stories in the Kenyan press on Wednesday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- Six armed robbers stage a daring robbery at Standard Chartered Bank Kenya Ltd, taking off with 96 million shillings ($1.7 million).
- Businessman Kamlesh Pattni is allowed to travel abroad but only on condition that he be accompanied by an officer from the criminal investigation department.
- Supporters of the ruling Kenya African National Union are angered by a decision to nominate a by-election candiate through the delegates system.
- Gangsters raid a market in western Kenya, murder four people and wound another before disappearing.
- Public universities will restructure their courses to ensure more students take the programmes of their choice.
- Meteorological department staff say they will strike next Friday in solidarity with air traffic controllers.
- Three opposition members of parliament led by Paul Muite are in Kigali, Rwanda on an undisclosed mission.
- U.S. Ambassador to Kenya Prudence Bushnell says her government rejects the notion that the opposition should be assisted by the U.S. to bring about changes in Kenya.
- Some senior government officials are accused of violating procedures for issuing new identity cards. ($1=54 Kenyan Shillings)
